history.summary: A 1,227 sqft 4BR (the smallest of FLO Residence's 88-unit 4BR type) at $1.835M / $1,496 psf. The ask is at-to-slightly-above fair value once the project's own size tiers are separated properly — not the discount the 756 score implies. The score is carried by a trailing 8.23% CAGR (the one-off 2021-26 Punggol repricing off a $992 psf base, now decelerating) plus an MRT credit that is wrong: the 240m station is Coral Edge LRT; the nearest MRT is Punggol at 1,895m. Correct that one input and score_1000 falls to roughly 643 — below the 650 gate that selected this listing.
history.rating_rationale: Priced fairly, with no edge in either direction. Indexing FLO's own liquid 1,012 sqft cohort (Nov-24 $1,374 psf -> Feb-26 $1,463-1,502, +7-9% over 15 months) onto the single 1,227 sqft print (Nov-24, $1.65M / $1,345 psf, fl 11-15) implies ~$1,450 psf today; the adjacent 4BR 1,346 sqft cohort (Sep-25 $1,908k / $1,418 psf) plus the normal size gradient implies ~$1,480-1,500. The $1,496 ask sits at the top of that band and would set a project record for the 1,227 sqft type (+11% over the last print). The algo's two price flags are directionally right but overstated: ask_above_own_stack_prints (+16%, n=7) pools 3BR PES stock into the comp set - the developer mix shows 1,152-1,356 sqft IS the '3-bedroom PES' type (8 units), and two of those seven prints are fl 01-05 at $843 and $1,172 psf; psf_premium_vs_ura_median_pct (+10.9%) compares a 4BR against a median dominated by 764-1,012 sqft stock, a size-mix artifact. Cleaned up, the true premium is ~+3%, not +16%. But correcting the flags down only moves this from overpriced to fully priced. Against that: gross yield is ~3.0-3.1% and the DB's $4,800 rent assumption sits above the top of realsmart's latest 12 contracts ($3,300-$4,350, median $4,050, all of them 2BR/3BR); MRT access is LRT-only at 1.9km to Punggol NEL; and the exit cohort for this size is thin (psf_cohort_txns=4, one 1,227 sqft print in 24 months, 88 4BR units vs 160 of the liquid 3BR Premium type). The relative_value -3.6% 'cheap for its age' read is a geography artifact - D19's $1,693 median blends Serangoon/Kovan/Hougang with Punggol. Supporting the floor, not the upside: realsmart REALSCORE 3.8/5 with 98.1% profitable on a deep 268 matched resale pairs (263 profitable / 5 unprofitable, avg holding 7.4yrs, $59.8M total profits, 789 lifetime transactions, 50+ deals in the past year) - genuine downside evidence that this project has essentially never lost an owner money, but backward-looking and single-regime: 79% sold at launch around $900-1,000 psf and exited into the 2021-26 boom. A buyer today at $1,496 psf gets none of that cushion. At a realistic 4.0%/yr (OCR baseline; realized forward OCR is +3.7%) the all-cash 5yr annualized ROI is ~3.9%. Sound asset, right region, broad sub-$2M HDB-upgrader buyer pool, 84yrs lease - but nothing here to underwrite outperformance. Not an Avoid (no capital-impairment risk, no material overpayment); simply no reason to transact.

history.summary: A 1,012 sqft 3BR at FLO Residence (Punggol, D19, 99yr from Dec-2011) asking $1.55M / $1,532 psf. The unit type is the project's most liquid — 11 of 14 same-size prints in 24 months — and the downside record is among the deepest available anywhere: 98.1% of 268 matched resale pairs sold at a profit. But the ask is a project RECORD: it sits above the highest same-size price ($1,520,000) and PSF ($1,519) FLO has ever printed, and above the project's entire 12-month range. Indexed forward from the last comparable print it is roughly fair, not cheap — there is no margin of safety, and the 776 score that selected this listing is inflated by ~100 points by an MRT input that is actually an LRT.
history.rating_rationale: Not a Buy because the buyer captures no discount and sets a project high-water mark. FLO's tight same-size cohort (941-1,083 sqft, 24mo, n=14) has a median of $1,412 psf / $1,428,888 and a MAXIMUM of $1,519 psf / $1,520,000; this ask is +8.5% over the median and +0.9% above the highest PSF ever recorded for the type. Indexing the most recent comparable print (Feb-2026, 1,012 sqft, fl 06-10, $1,520,000 / $1,502 psf) forward five months at the cohort's own ~5%/yr same-size drift gives ~$1,534 psf — so $1,532 is approximately fair value, and fair value is the whole of the case. Not an Avoid because the fundamentals underneath the price are sound: the type is genuinely liquid, the bedroom count is real (URA rental bands 950-1,150 sqft on 157 contracts - verdict ok, no relabel), 84 years of lease means no decay drag over a 5-7yr hold, the $1.55M quantum sits in the HDB-upgrader band that supplies 66% of FLO's buyers, and OCR/D19 is the strongest forward region in the backtest. The score_1000 of 776 should not be read as cheapness: correcting the MRT field alone takes it to ~678, and re-scoring at a defensible 4%/yr forward rate with a realistic $4,100 rent takes it to 567 - below the recommended tier. FLO is the cheapest private condo in Punggol ($1,463 median vs Watertown $1,718, Parc Centros $1,714, A Treasure Trove $1,638 over the last 12 months of URA resale prints), but that gap is a persistent LRT-only/traffic-noise location level, not a discount that is closing - the same trap as reading a Choa Chu Kang project as cheap-for-D23.
red_flags: Ask is a project record: $1,550,000 / $1,532 psf exceeds the highest same-size print FLO has ever recorded ($1,520,000 / $1,519 psf, Feb-2026) and sits above the project's ENTIRE 12-month print range ($1,284-$1,519 psf, n=11). The buyer sets the new high rather than buying into an existing one.

MRT credit in the scored record is wrong, same defect found in the FLO 4BR eval today: nearest_mrt_distance_m=240 is Coral Edge PE3, an LRT, which the DB's own mrt_info field states verbatim ('3 min (220 m) from PE3 Coral Edge LRT Station') and realsmart confirms (Coral Edge 173m LRT, Riviera 345m LRT, Meridian 689m LRT - no MRT listed). The nearest MRT is Punggol NEL at ~1,895m, which the scorer's own geocoder independently resolves. MMR credits +5.8 where the true distance scores -8.67, a 14.5-point swing: score_1000 776 -> ~678.

The score's largest positive (appreciation +12.69, from an 8.23% trailing CAGR) is a de-weighted signal under the repo's own priors, and it overstates the clean evidence. FLO's annual median PSF ran $992 (2021) -> $1,136 -> $1,246 -> $1,314 -> $1,412 -> $1,474 (2026), i.e. +4.4% in the latest year with momentum at -0.577; the like-for-like same-size, same-floor-tier series (fl 06-10, 1,012 sqft) runs $1,384 (Dec-24) -> $1,502 (Feb-26), about +7%/yr and flattening. The pooled 8.23% is partly the 2021-26 Punggol repricing off a depressed base.

Thin carry: at the DB's $4,200/mo the gross yield is 3.25%, but $4,200 is the TOP of the realistic band - realsmart's latest 12 contracts show a $4,050 median across a $3,300-$4,350 range, with the two Jun-2026 3BR contracts at 1,000-1,100 sqft printing $4,000 and $4,200. A central $4,050-4,100 puts gross at ~3.15% and net near 2.0%.

Very heavy competing rental supply: 61 rental contracts logged in the past month against 530 units (~11.5% of the project). Whatever the exact window, FLO is an investor-heavy block where a landlord competes with many near-identical 3BRs, which caps rent growth.

relative_value of -1.2% vs the age-adjusted D19 median is a within-district geography artifact, not value: the D19 median of $1,693 psf blends Serangoon/Kovan/Hougang with Punggol. Against the correct peer set - Punggol private resale - the subject is not cheap for what it is.

No floor level disclosed, and the cohort shows floor is NOT a reliable premium at FLO (fl 01-05 printed $1,482 psf in Jun-2025 while fl 16-20 printed $1,374 psf in Nov-2024; the large high-floor units print $921-$1,090 psf). So a high floor cannot be assumed to justify the record ask, and a low/poorly-facing unit cannot be ruled out.

history.summary: The 1,227 sqft 4BR at FLO Residence (Punggol, D19, 99yr from Dec-2011, 530 units) that was judged Neutral at $1.835M on 29-Jul-2026 (listing 500210984) has been RELISTED at $1,888,000 / $1,539 psf on 18-Sep-2026 - a +2.9% price RAISE, not a cut. In between, the only 2026 print of this exact size cleared at $1,800,000 / $1,467 psf (21-Jul-2026, realsmart), so the seller has moved the ask from ~+2% to ~+5% above the latest same-size transaction. Size-adjusting the Sep-2025 1,345 sqft print ($1,418 psf, fl 06-10) forward puts fair for a 1,227 sqft unit at roughly $1,470-1,500 psf, i.e. $1.80-1.84M. The 737 score that pulled this through the gate is carried by a trailing 8.23% CAGR (de-weighted signal) and a +5.04 MRT component that is actually the Coral Edge LRT; correcting the MRT input alone takes score_1000 to roughly 630, under the 650 gate. The project's downside record is genuinely deep (REALSCORE 3.8, 98.2% of 274 resale pairs profitable), but that is evidence that prior cohorts bought well, not that this ask is fair. Overpriced by ~5% on a thin 4-print cohort with 1.7% net carry: Avoid at $1.888M; it becomes a fair Neutral only at or under the $1.80M July print.
history.rating_rationale: Ask $1,888,000 / $1,539 psf is ~4.9% above the only 2026 print of this exact 1,227 sqft size ($1,800,000 / $1,467 psf, 21-Jul-2026) and ~14% above the tight-cohort prints district-indexed in the repo (ask_above_own_stack_prints, n=7). The seller RAISED the ask +2.9% from the $1.835M July listing after that $1.80M print cleared - the reverse-cut relist pattern where the earlier price was the honest anchor. Carry is negative on leverage (3.05% gross / 1.71% net on a $4,800 rent from only 5 contracts), the same-size exit cohort is thin (psf_cohort_txns=4; four 1,227 sqft prints ever), floor and facing are undisclosed in a project with recorded traffic-noise complaints, and the score is overstated by ~100 points of LRT-counted-as-MRT credit. Confidence is medium rather than high because the July print's floor is unknown and a top-floor unit could justify part of the premium - but nothing in the listing supports it, and the burden is on the ask.

Ask sits ~4.9% above the latest same-size print: realsmart records a 1,227 sqft resale at $1,800,000 / $1,467 psf on 21-Jul-2026 - the only 2026 print of this size. The repo's URA file (ends Sep-25 for FLO) has the prior 1,227 sqft print at $1,650,000 / $1,345 psf (Nov-24, fl 11-15); ask_above_own_stack_prints fires at +18% district-indexed (n=7).

Fair value for 1,227 sqft today is ~$1,470-1,500 psf ($1.80-1.84M): the Sep-25 1,345 sqft print at $1,418 psf (fl 06-10), size-adjusted (+~2% for the smaller size at elasticity -0.19) and indexed ~4%/yr, lands near $1,500; the Jul-26 print at $1,467 confirms it. $1,539 is 3-5% over.

Score is overstated: nearest_mrt_distance_m=320 is Coral Edge PE3 LRT (the DB's own mrt_info says so verbatim); nearest MRT is Punggol NEL ~1.9km. MMR mrt +5.04 should be ~-8.7, a ~13.7-pt MMR swing taking score_1000 from 737 to roughly 630 - BELOW the 650 gate that selected this listing. The next-largest component, appreciation +10.15, rests on the trailing 8.23% 5yr CAGR - the 2021-26 Punggol repricing off a ~$1,000 psf base, decelerating (momentum -0.577, +4-5% latest year).

Thin exit cohort for this size: psf_cohort_txns=4; only four 1,227 sqft prints in the entire URA history (Jul-21, Aug-21, Jun-22, Nov-24) plus the Jul-26 realsmart print. FLO's liquid stock is the 926-1,012 sqft 3BR (160 Premium 3BRs alone); the 88-unit 4BR type transacts ~once a year per size. 'very_deep' buyer pool is a district read, not a unit-type read.

Negative carry on leverage: $4,800/mo rent (ura_project_bed, only 5 contracts in 12mo, confidence 0.61, rental_cache 100d stale) gives 3.05% gross / 1.71% net. realsmart's latest 12 leases are all 2BR/3BR at $3,500-4,650 (median $4,250); no recent 4BR contract confirms $4,800.

relative_value -0.8% vs the age-adjusted D19 size-band median ($1,551) is a geography artifact: D19's $1,693 median blends Serangoon/Kovan/Hougang with Punggol. Against Punggol private resale and the project's own prints the unit is a premium, not at-par.

Floor level and facing undisclosed; no stack profile (status not_researched). Floor moves psf materially in the large-unit cohort (1,345 sqft: $1,249 fl 01-05 vs $1,418 fl 06-10 vs $1,356 fl 16-20), and EdgeProp carries a resident review of traffic noise severe enough to keep windows and balcony doors shut - facing is a material unverified risk.

1,227 sqft is below the 4BR band's own floor in URA rental filings (band 1,250-1,350 on 16 contracts; bed_bands 'ok' only via the 12% tolerance) and below 99.co's published 4BR range of 1,345-1,485 sqft - the smallest 4BR format. Verify it is a true 4-bedder and not a 3BR+study before paying a 4BR price.
Heavy identical supply: 19 units listed for sale project-wide (PropertyGuru), including three other 4BRs in the DB at $1.83M-$2.00M; the buyer has alternatives inside the same block.
catalysts: Deep downside record at project level: REALSCORE 3.8/5, 98.2% profitable across 274 matched resale pairs (269 profitable / 5 unprofitable), avg holding 7.5 yrs, avg annualized profit 5.4%, 795 total transactions - far past the 150-pair trust threshold. Backward-looking: it says prior cohorts entered well, not that this ask is fair.
OCR / D19 is the strongest forward region in the backtest (realized fwd OCR +3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%); sub-$2M 4BR quantum sits in the HDB-upgrader band (FLO's buyer base ~66% HDB).
86 years of lease remaining (99 from Dec-2011); project age 10 sits inside the 7-30yr forward-return plateau - no age or lease-decay drag over a 5-7yr hold.

A negotiated price at or below the $1,800,000 July print (~$1,467 psf) removes the overpricing and would make this a fair Neutral - the seller's own July ask of $1.835M was already at the top of fair.
Greendale Primary, Mee Toh School and Horizon Primary within ~800m; Punggol Digital District supports the family-tenant catchment - narrative only, zero measured forward power.

At $4,800: 3.05% gross, 1.71% net; a realistic $4,500-4,700 puts gross at ~2.9-3.0%. 3BR rents have been flat since 2023; a 4BR competes for a thin family-tenant pool with no expat depth in an investor-heavy 530-unit block (~60 leases/month project-wide).
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Trailing 8.23% 5yr CAGR (130 txns) is the one-off 2021-26 Punggol repricing: annual median psf $1,002 -> $1,136 -> $1,246 -> $1,314 -> $1,412 -> $1,474 (2026), i.e. +4-5% in the latest year and decelerating (momentum -0.577). Forward, use the OCR baseline (~3.7%/yr); the 1,227 sqft series ($1,345 Nov-24 -> $1,467 Jul-26, ~+5.5%/yr) is consistent with that, but the buyer at $1,539 psf starts ~5% ahead of the last print and needs ~1.3 years of that growth just to reach par.
